content: Atovaquone is a medication used to prevent or treat a severe lung infection known as Pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP). It is available in oral suspension form and is commonly marketed under the brand name Mepron. How to Use: Shake the bottle gently but thoroughly before each dose. For treating PCP, take the medication orally with food as directed by your doctor, typically twice daily for 21 days. For preventing PCP, take the medication with food, usually once daily as prescribed. If prescribed twice daily, take it approximately 12 hours apart. Complete the full course of treatment, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Dosage: For treatment: 750 mg orally twice daily for 21 days. For prophylaxis: 1500 mg daily, either as a single dose or divided into two doses, taken with food. Pediatric Use: For children under 13 years, the safety and efficacy of atovaquone have not been established. For children over 13 years, the recommended dose is 750 mg (5 mL) twice daily (total daily dose of 1500 mg) with food for 21 days. Side Effects: Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, dizziness, difficulty sleeping, and a runny nose. A mild rash may occur, which is usually not serious. However, it is important to distinguish this from a rare rash that could indicate a severe allergic reaction. Serious allergic reactions, such as bronchospasm, angioedema, throat tightness, or urticaria, are rare but require immediate medical attention. Precautions: Inform your doctor if you are allergic to atovaquone or any of its components. This medication may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Atovaquone may cause dizziness. Limit alcohol and marijuana use, as these can exacerbate dizziness. During pregnancy, use this medication only if clearly needed. It is unknown if atovaquone passes into breast milk, so use caution if breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Atovaquone may interact with other medications, potentially altering its effectiveness or increasing the risk of side effects. Examples include: Efavirenz: Reduces atovaquone levels; avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin and Rifabutin: Decrease atovaquone levels by increasing metabolism; use caution and monitor closely. Metoclopramide: May reduce atovaquone absorption; monitor for reduced therapeutic effects. Tetracycline: May decrease atovaquone levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption; monitor closely. Warfarin: Atovaquone may increase the effects of warfarin; use caution and monitor. Avoid co-administration of topical dapsone with oral dapsone or antimalarial medications due to the risk of hemolytic reactions. Storage: Store at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Do not freeze the product, as freezing reduces the amount of atovaquone your body can absorb, potentially decreasing its effectiveness. Properly discard expired or unused medication. Do not flush it down the toilet or pour it into a drain unless instructed to do so. Overdose: In case of overdose with serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. Important Notes: This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other conditions unless directed by your doctor. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Additional Information: Atovaquone is highly protein-bound (>99%) and undergoes enterohepatic recirculation. Its bioavailability is 23% for tablets and 47% for suspension. The elimination half-life is 2-3 days, and it is primarily excreted unchanged in feces (94%). The medication inhibits the electron transport chain in Plasmodium species, which is its mechanism of action. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
